entities.description: Weekly (later daily) Black newspaper founded in Chicago in 1905; anchor of the Sengstacke chain; digital-only after July 10, 2019.
entities.name: The Chicago Defender
entities.significance: Central subject of the brief; the distribution system under study.

entities.description: Founder of the Chicago Defender (1905); lawyer and publisher; built the paper into the highest-circulation Black newspaper in the country.
entities.name: Robert Sengstacke Abbott
entities.significance: Architect of the paper and its early distribution strategy.

entities.description: Abbott's nephew and successor as publisher; took the paper daily in 1956; built the Sengstacke newspaper chain.
entities.name: John H. Sengstacke
entities.significance: Extended the Defender's footprint via chain ownership and the daily edition.

entities.description: Black railroad sleeping-car porters, employed by the Pullman Company; acted as the Defender's unofficial circulation agents in the South.
entities.name: Pullman porters
entities.significance: Core informal distribution channel into the Jim Crow South.

entities.description: Labor union founded 1925 under A. Philip Randolph; organized the porters who carried the Defender.
entities.name: Brotherhood of Sleeping Car Porters
entities.significance: Labor context of the carrier network.

entities.description: Federal official whose 1920 report 'Negro Migration During the War' documented Southern reception of the Defender.
entities.name: Emmett J. Scott
entities.significance: Primary-source witness to distribution's reception effects.

entities.description: Defender staffer photographed at work in the paper's office; visual anchor for the newsroom behind the network.
entities.name: L. Alex Wilson
entities.significance: Human face of the Defender newsroom (rights-cleared image).

entities.description: Defender editor fired by John Sengstacke in 1964 over civil-rights coverage; the firing was tracked in an FBI memo.
entities.name: C. Sumner Stone
entities.significance: Subject of the FBI surveillance memo; evidence of the paper's perceived influence.

entities.description: Defender publisher at the digital transition; reported web readership of several hundred thousand vs. print under 20,000.
entities.name: Hiram Jackson
entities.significance: Voice of the digital-distribution era.

entities.description: Owner of the Defender from January 2003; Sengstacke-era successor company.
entities.name: Real Times Media
entities.significance: Post-2003 owner; steward of the print-to-digital transition.

entities.description: Sister papers in the Sengstacke chain (Detroit, Memphis, Pittsburgh); shared ownership and content circulation.
entities.name: Sengstacke chain papers (Michigan Chronicle, Tri-State Defender, New Pittsburgh Courier)
entities.significance: Multi-city editorial footprint; distinct from formal syndication.

entities.description: Railroad running Chicago to New Orleans; the principal corridor of the porter distribution network.
entities.name: Illinois Central Railroad
entities.significance: Physical infrastructure of the porter network.

entities.description: Archive holding the Abbott-Sengstacke Family Papers (83 boxes, ~4,000 photos, ~100 home movies), including business records.
entities.name: Harsh Collection, Chicago Public Library
entities.significance: Priority archival target for unresolved distribution mechanics.

entities.description: Federal legislative record; source of the porter-network tribute and the 1929 circulation figure.
entities.name: Congressional Record
entities.significance: Government-record corroboration of the porter network.

entities.description: Federal agency whose 1964 memorandum on the Defender survives in a public-domain Internet Archive file.
entities.name: Federal Bureau of Investigation
entities.significance: Surveilled the Defender; backhanded evidence of reach.

entities.description: Chicago PBS member station; producer of 'Chicago Stories: Pullman and the Railroad Rebellion' (2023).
entities.name: WTTW
entities.significance: Institutional video source on the porter network.

entities.description: 1953 All-American Newsreel episode on the Black press; segment 5 tours the Defender composing room.
entities.name: One Tenth of a Nation — The Press (1953)
entities.significance: Archival moving-image evidence of the Defender's production plant.

entities.description: FSA-OWI photographer who photographed a Defender newsboy in Chicago, April 1942.
entities.name: Jack Delano
entities.significance: Visual evidence of the street-vendor layer.

entities.description: Bronzeville newsstand (bought 1945) that sold the Defender alongside the Tribune and Sun-Times.
entities.name: Rodgers News Stand
entities.significance: Documented neighborhood retail node.

entities.description: Author of 'The Defender' (2016); former Defender reporter (1991-1996); lecturer at UChicago Harris School.
entities.name: Ethan Michaeli
entities.significance: Historian-author video source on the Defender's influence.
